prayerExcerpt.en-US: With the saints the great end for which they lived was always present to their minds, and they thought every moment lost in which they did not make some advances toward eternal bliss.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Para os santos, o grande fim para o qual viviam estava sempre presente em suas mentes, e julgavam perdido todo momento em que não faziam algum avanço rumo à bem-aventurança eterna.

meta.face: A Roman woman of about twenty with a fair olive complexion and a LONG, RECTANGULAR face with SOFT corners — a smooth forehead with the dark hair growing to a small WIDOW'S PEAK at its centre, a LONG, STRAIGHT nose, DEEP-SET, calm dark-brown eyes under LOW, STRAIGHT dark brows, flat cheeks, a SHORT upper lip over a small, full, closed mouth, a small, SQUARE chin; dark hair parted from the peak and drawn back under the veil; the gaze level and recollected, toward us.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book tells a holy virgin 'among the disciples of the apostles', said to be St. Peter's daughter though 'it seems not certain whether St. Petronilla was more than the spiritual daughter of that apostle', buried on the way to Ardea; its engraving shows a haloed young woman seated by a boat at the shore. Wikipedia says the kinship came from a misread inscription and that she was probably of the family of the Aurelii; her grave in the catacomb of Domitilla, with a painting of her receiving the deceased Veneranda into heaven, confirms the old cult. The card follows the catacomb dress and shows no kinship; the long, rectangular face with the widow's peak is our choice.
